new_defect_types.name: unrequested_slogan_text
new_defect_types.description: Well-spelled motivational or thematic slogans that nobody asked for, used as set dressing on billboards, banners and bins ('A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'HUMANITY PERSISTS'). Often the same phrase repeats across several signs in one image.
examples: phi112/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'PLASTICS SHAPE A BRIGHTER TOMORROW' + 'BETTER PARTS A STRONGER TOMORROW'
orig593/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'A BRIGHTER TOMORROW' on two billboards
orig479/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: 'HUMANITY PERSISTS', 'A CLEANER TOMORROW SOMEDAY'
phi353/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: 'PEOPLE TECHNOLOGY A BRIGHTER TOMORROW'
phi239/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: 'BUILD A BETTER TOMORROW'
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A03 catches only pseudo-text. B04 covers only quoted prompt text and prompt-word leakage. B07 covers only extras that change the scene. Well-formed but editorialising text falls between all three. It is a strong fingerprint of one model family (5/9 prompts).

new_defect_types.name: wrong_symbol_or_icon
new_defect_types.description: A pictogram, icon or standard symbol is wrong for the object it sits on, even when the text is spelled correctly. Examples are a road-sign glyph whose meaning contradicts the sign text, or a nonsense icon.
examples: phi477/gpt_image_2: two-way-traffic arrows on a DIVIDED HIGHWAY BEGINS sign
phi477/krea2_turbo: pedestrian icon
phi477/qwen_image_2p1_nope: pickup-truck icon
phi477/fibo2_dev: 'H' glyph
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A02/A03 judge letters only. B02 is about objects. Icons and standard symbols have no home, so judges pass these signs as 'text correct'.

new_defect_types.name: technical_term_literalism
new_defect_types.description: A technical or compound term is drawn by its literal words instead of what it means in the domain.
examples: phi239/flux3_klein_base: 'cable chains' drawn as drooping metal link chains
phi239/krea2_turbo: concrete 'beads' as rows of balls, with pellets spilled at the base
phi353/qwen_image_2p1_nope: 'brain-computer interface' headset drawn as a brain-textured cap
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B02 says 'right kind, including real-world object', but judges treat the literal object as matching the noun. An explicit rule that domain terms are judged by their domain meaning is needed.

new_defect_types.name: functional_logic_violation
new_defect_types.description: A scene breaks the operating rules of the domain. Examples are a vehicle in the opposing lanes driving away from the camera (wrong-way), a person inside a robot cell with no guard, or a robot outside its own enclosure.
examples: phi477/flux3_klein_base: pickup on the opposing side of the new median, seen from behind
phi353/krea2_turbo: operator handles the bracket the robot is gripping, no screen
phi353/qwen_image_2p1_pe: robot outside the glass enclosure
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A19 covers out-of-place objects and A12 physics. Rule or affordance violations (traffic direction, safety guarding) are not named, so judges miss them.

rubric_issues.problem: The prompt asks for unquoted text ('elegant printed text' on book pages). Neither A02 (intended) nor A03 (incidental) clearly applies, and severity differs.
examples: orig230/flux3_klein, qwen_image_2p1_nope: full pages of pseudo-text
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Requested but unspecified text: judge legibility under A03 with severity one step higher (moderate when it covers a focal surface). There is no B04 because there is no target string.

rubric_issues.problem: Prompts with negations ('thornless', 'no sharp accessories') are often violated (spines). v2 gives no severity anchor, so judges treat spines as natural cactus detail.
examples: orig116/krea2_turbo: long spines everywhere
orig116/ideogram4_nf4, qwen_image_2p1_nope
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add to B05/B07: an explicitly negated attribute that is present on the focal subject is at least moderate, and major when it is prominent across the subject.

rubric_issues.problem: 'looking up at', 'gazing at' are judged from the head pose. The pupils often point elsewhere.
examples: orig355/qwen_image_2p1_nope: giant's pupils look away from the hamster
orig355/flux3_klein: both characters look at the camera
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: For a requested gaze, trace the pupil and head direction to the target. Looking at the camera counts as a miss.

rubric_issues.problem: Prompt adjectives turned into in-scene signage are missed because B04 reads like a caption rule.
examples: orig479/gemini_3_1_flash_image: 'NEON CHAOS', 'RUSTY PATH' neon signs
orig593/fibo2_dev: 'Guardian 383349' billboard
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: State that B04 leakage includes signs, billboards and labels that restate prompt words or the quoted string somewhere other than the requested location.

rubric_issues.problem: Photoreal industrial prompts get real OEM branding on almost every gpt/gemini image (FANUC, KUKA, ARBURG, NISSEI, COBOD, EMOTIV), sometimes with the wrong model number ('HITACHI SE180DU').
examples: phi112/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high
phi239/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Keep C01 as a flag but add a sub-flag 'brand_model_mismatch'. A wrong pairing is a factual error that could go to Layer A (A19) as well.

rubric_issues.problem: Small AI-provenance sparkle marks look like glints and are not listed.
examples: phi353/ideogram4_nf4: four-point sparkle at bottom-right
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Name 'generator provenance marks (sparkle/star logos in a corner)' under A16, always at least moderate.

false_positive_traps.description: Correct non-Latin text in cyberpunk scenes is easy to over-flag as pseudo-text. Read the script before calling A03.
examples: orig479/gpt_image_2: '未来は死んだ' is correct Japanese
orig479/qwen_image_2p1_pe: '未来已死', '機械' are correct

false_positive_traps.description: Requested reflections can look like ghost duplicates.
examples: phi353/qwen_image_2p1_nope: faint reflection of the head cap on the safety glass (requested 'subtle reflections')
phi477/gpt_image_2_quality_high: reflection of the sign on the car hood

false_positive_traps.description: Prompt-mandated impossibilities are not A12: lava poured onto a flower that does not burn, a hologram floating beside the chest.
examples: orig479 all models
orig593/flux3_klein_base: screen floating off the chest

false_positive_traps.description: Insect leg counts on thin or partly occluded legs are unreliable at 1024px. Flag B01 only when the count is clearly not 6.
examples: orig230: most butterflies show 4-6 visible legs with others hidden behind wings

false_positive_traps.description: Stylised character limbs (a cactus arm ending in a rounded fold, a cactus with stubby legs) are style choices in non-photographic mode, not A04/A05 defects.

orig116/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high
